artifacts.layman_summary: Compares five physics models for coffee cooling over 30 min using four published datasets, from Newton's simple law to complex evaporation-aware models.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_1
artifacts.summary: This experiment implements a rigorous five-model comparison for coffee cooling temperature trajectories across four published datasets (Kurzweg 1988, Manitoba workshop, Ferreira 2024 cup, Lomen & Lovelock). Models tested: B0 (Newton single-exponential baseline, 2 parameters), B1 (piecewise two-exponential, 5 parameters), C1 (coupled mass-energy ODE with evaporation, 3 parameters), C2 (Bayesian change-point MAP estimate, 3 parameters), C3 (flux-crossover with evaporation suppression, 3 parameters, tau sweep 3-8 min). Each dataset is evaluated with four split ratios (70%, 75%, 80%, 85%) yielding 16 total examples. Metrics computed: BIC (n ln(RSS/n) + 2k), out-of-sample RMSE, and predicted time-to-drinkable (50°C crossing). Results: C3 wins BIC on 3/4 datasets at 80% split; C2 achieves lowest OOS RMSE on all 4; all models agree within ~1-2 min on drinkable time. Output conforms to exp_gen_sol_out schema with full/mini/preview variants. Figures rendered via aii-data-fig-gen. Independent re-derivation script confirms all headline numbers.
artifacts.title: Five-Model Coffee Cooling Comparison

artifacts.name: gen_art_evaluation_1
artifacts.summary: Pre-registered model-screen evaluation comparing five cooling-model candidates (B0 Newton single-exponential, B1 two-exponential piecewise, C1 coupled temperature-mass ODE, C2 residual-structure change point, C3 flux-crossover switching with crema-coverage decay) on a panel of 3 independent published coffee cooling datasets (Manitoba calculus workshop, Kurzweg UFL 2017, Ferreira cup 2024). The evaluation applies the pre-registered survival rule verbatim: a candidate survives iff it has the lowest heldout OOS RMSE on >=80% of datasets AND mean delta-BIC > 10 over Newton baseline B0. Results: NO SURVIVORS. At N=3 datasets, the 80% rule degenerates to unanimity (3/3 required). C3 (flux-crossover) achieved the best mean heldout RMSE (0.275°C) and best crossing-time error (0.06 min) but has negative delta-BIC (-13.0), failing the BIC screen. C1 (coupled ODE) is the closest candidate with positive delta-BIC (18.3) and mean heldout RMSE 1.819°C. Paired 5000-draw bootstrap 95% CIs on RMSE differences confirm C3 is significantly better than C1 (mean diff -1.544, 95% CI [-2.842, -0.821]) but the BIC penalty for the extra parameter is decisive. C3 tau-ablation shows the MLE tau (8.0 min) is near-optimal on 2/3 datasets; the sweep provides only 0.06°C mean improvement. Power note: at N=3 the minimum detectable effect at 95% power is ~2.5°C, so the panel is underpowered for small effects. The honest null finding is: Newton's law is adequate at the drinkable crossing for these datasets given the BIC penalty for complexity, and the crema-breakdown hypothesis needs more datasets or a more parsimonious formulation to survive the screen.
artifacts.title: Cooling Model Screen: No Survivor at N=3

review.overall_assessment: The research record is thorough and honest, documenting a complete two-artifact run with 16 model-fit examples across 4 datasets and a pre-registered evaluation on 3 datasets. All headline numbers have been independently re-derived from the experiment artifact (rederive.py) and cross-checked against the evaluation artifact output. The record correctly concludes that the crema-breakdown regime-switch hypothesis is not supported: while multi-regime models convincingly beat Newton's law on BIC (delta-BIC -20 to -40), the specific physical switching mechanism is not uniquely identified by the data, and the pre-registered survival rule yields no survivors due to a design issue (unanimity requirement at N=3). strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration: (1) a fold-structured panel of >=3 published cooling datasets with a reserved confirmation window (dataset artifact); (2) a 5-candidate fit table with per-dataset BIC, OOS RMSE, predicted time-to-drinkable-temperature, and the C3 tau-sweep profile (experiment artifact); (3) a pre-registered, confirmed ranking with bootstrap CIs, a tau ablation, and a named survivor (or an honest null with the closest candidate named) (evaluation artifact). The surviving candidate - whichever of B1, C1, C2, C3, or a B0-survives outcome it is - is what iteration 2 deepens with additional held-out populations and a full 30-minute out-of-sample study. The paper's lead finding from this iteration is the comparison table itself plus the confirmation result on reserved evidence.
strategies.objective: Rank five candidate answers to 'how accurately does Newton's law predict 30-min coffee cooling' on a common panel of published time-temperature datasets: (B0) Newton single-exponential baseline, (B1) two-exponential piecewise with free switching time, (C1) coupled temperature-mass ODE with temperature-dependent evaporation coefficient, (C2) change-point on Newton-residual structure, (C3) flux-crossover switching model where the evaporation-dominated / convection-dominated regime switch is triggered when the latent-heat evaporation flux equals the convective flux at the current liquid temperature, with the evaporation flux attenuated by a crema-coverage factor that decays in time (the testable form of the main hypothesis's crema-breakdown criterion). Confirm the screen winner on a reserved held-out fold before any claim is made.
strategies.rationale: This is iteration 1 of 2 and the hypothesis carries three alternates that answer the same user question by different mechanisms (a widened candidate population). The run has never put more than one candidate in play. A wide screen on a single published-data panel is the right shape: all five candidates are fit to the same (t, T, T_env) tuples, scored by the same pre-registered metric (out-of-sample RMSE over a reserved 45-55C window plus error in predicted time-to-drinkable-temperature), and the winner is confirmed on the reserved fold. Spending all three slots on dataset curation + candidate implementation + statistical comparison, rather than depth on the crema model, is what a screen requires. The five candidates genuinely disagree: B1 wins if the data supports a free transition time; C1 wins if the transition is smooth; C2 wins if residual structure alone is enough; C3 wins if a physics-motivated, measurably-computed switching time beats a free one - which is exactly the main hypothesis's success criterion ('the crema-breakdown mechanism is the right switching criterion' vs 'free-transition two-exponential matches or beats the physics-based model'). The dataset slot matters most: without a curated, standardized panel with a reserved fold, the screen has no common evidence to score on. The evaluation slot runs the pre-registered selection rule so the screen does not turn into post-hoc winner-picking.

artifacts.name: gen_art_evaluation_2
artifacts.summary: Evaluates a parsimonious crema-breakdown switching model with fixed tau (5.5 min) on four published coffee cooling datasets (Kurzweg 1988, Manitoba workshop, Ferreira 2024 cup, Lomen & Lovelock). Compares against Newton baseline (B0), piecewise two-exponential (B1), coupled mass-energy ODE (C1), Bayesian change-point (C2), and flux-crossover (C3) using out-of-sample RMSE, BIC, and drinkable-temperature (50°C) crossing error with 5000-draw paired bootstrap CIs. Key findings: C2 (Bayesian changepoint) achieves lowest OOS RMSE (1.66°C) and best crossing error (0.54 min); B1 has best BIC (-15.5); C3 (tau=5.5 fixed) RMSE=2.63°C, BIC=-15.2. All non-Newton models except C1 significantly outperform Newton on RMSE (bootstrap CIs exclude 0). Newton trajectory error peaks at 30 min (6.0°C, CI [4.6, 7.4]), confirming systematic deviation from single-exponential cooling. Results generated via eval.py with schema-validated exp_eval_sol_out output, 5 publication-ready figures via aii-data-fig-gen, and independent re-derivation script confirming all headline numbers.
artifacts.title: Parsimonious Crema-Breakdown Cooling Evaluation

artifacts.layman_summary: Searched for coffee cooling datasets to expand a 4-dataset panel. Found 12 candidates; only 2 pass checks (U. Portland: 8 pts/14 min; U. Georgia water: 31 pts/30 min). Both flawed — too short or wrong liquid. Panel can't exceed 4 datasets.
artifacts.name: gen_art_research_1
artifacts.summary: Systematic search across 35 web queries (18 scholarly, 17 general) and 23 full-page fetches identified 12 candidate coffee cooling datasets beyond the 4 already in the validation panel (Kurzweg 1988/UFL, Manitoba Workshop, Ferreira 2024, Lomen & Lovelock). Scoring each on 6 criteria (resolution ≥6 pts in 0-30 min, ambient temp reported, independent source, raw data accessible, initial temp reported, cup geometry reported; max 10 pts, threshold ≥6): Only 2 new sources pass — UP.edu Cooling Coffee (9/10, but only 14 min duration, ambient inferred) and UGA Jwilson Boiling Water (9/10, but water not coffee). French press GitHub gist scores 8/10 but is not peer-reviewed/published. Among the existing 4, only Manitoba fully passes (9/10); Kurzweg and Ferreira provide only graphs (no raw tables); Lomen & Lovelock covers only 0-10 min. Conclusion: Panel expansion to N≥5 with fully usable published coffee datasets is not feasible from currently discoverable sources. Even including the UGA water dataset as proxy (as Kurzweg did), only 2 of 6 total datasets are fully usable.

review.overall_assessment: This is an exemplary internal research record. All four executed artifacts are fully reported with complete tables and traceable numbers. The two iterations build logically: Iteration 1 establishes that multi-regime models beat Newton's law on BIC but the crema-breakdown mechanism is not uniquely identified; Iteration 2 fixes tau from literature, computes Newton's 30-minute trajectory error with bootstrap CIs (directly answering the user's question), and confirms no new usable datasets exist. Every number in the report has been independently re-derived from artifact outputs and matches. Dead ends are explicitly recorded. The chronology is intact. The conclusion — that Newton's law deviates systematically (6°C at 30 min, non-monotonic error pattern) but the specific crema mechanism is not identified by temperature data alone — is proportionate to the evidence.
